depth.h2: What Highland Park Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: The median home in Highland Park was built in 1963, and about 1 in 4 went up before 1940. Add wooded ravines, mature trees and long Lake County winters, and the same few problems keep showing up.

tiles.title: Older Homes, Older Pipes
tiles.body: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, often with clay sewer pipe, cast iron drains and galvanized water lines. These materials wear out slowly, until a [small leak](/highland-park/leak-repairs) or a [tired water heater](/highland-park/water-heater-repair) turns into a bigger repair.

tiles.title: Ravines, Mature Trees and Your Sewer Line
tiles.body: Highland Park’s ravines and tree-lined streets are [hard on sewer lines](/highland-park/sewer-repair). Roots grow toward moisture and slip into older pipe through the joints. The first signs are slow drains or a gurgle when the washer empties.

tiles.title: Heavy Rain, Snowmelt and Basement Backups
tiles.body: Heavy rain and spring snowmelt can [push water into Highland Park basements](/highland-park/basement-flooding). A [backflow valve](/highland-park/sewage-line-backup-services) stops sewage from coming up through floor drains. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/highland-park/sump-pumps) keeps running when the power goes out. An [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems) lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen.

tiles.title: Hard Freezes and Burst Pipes
tiles.body: Lake County winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and they can [split and flood a basement](/highland-park/burst-pipe-repair) once they thaw. If you see water where it shouldn’t be, shut off your main valve and call us 24/7.

items.q: Can tree roots damage my sewer line?
items.preview: Yes, and it’s a real risk in a city with as many mature trees as Highland Park.
items.a: Yes, and it’s a real risk in a city with as many mature trees as Highland Park. Roots grow toward moisture and slip into sewer lines through cracks and loose joints, especially in older clay pipe. Early signs include slow drains, gurgling and backups in the lowest drain in the house. In Highland Park, homeowners own the private sewer line from the house to the city main, so a root problem there is yours to fix. A [camera inspection](/highland-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows whether roots are the cause, and [hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) or a sewer repair can clear them out.

items.q: My home was built before 1960. Is it at higher risk?
items.preview: It can be. About 45% of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940.
items.a: It can be. About 45% of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940. Homes from those years often have clay sewer pipe, cast iron drains or galvanized water lines, and all of them wear out with age. Age alone doesn’t mean something is wrong. [An inspection](/highland-park/plumbing-maintenance) tells you where your system stands, so you can plan repairs instead of reacting to a leak.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from sewer backups?
items.preview: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris.
items.a: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris. For homes with repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems) lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen. We can look at your setup and tell you which option makes sense for your home.

items.q: How often should I have my sewer line inspected?
items.preview: There’s no fixed schedule, but older homes with mature trees nearby benefit from a camera inspection every few years, or any time you notice slow drains or gurgling.
items.a: There’s no fixed schedule, but older homes with mature trees nearby benefit from a camera inspection every few years, or any time you notice slow drains or gurgling. Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, often with clay sewer pipe that roots get into more easily. An inspection shows the condition of your line so you can fix small problems early.
